content: Rifampin is a medication that works by eliminating bacteria responsible for causing tuberculosis (TB). It is typically used in combination with other drugs to treat TB or to eradicate Neisseria meningitidis, a type of bacteria, in order to prevent the spread of these infections to others. However, it is important to note that rifampin is not used to treat active Neisseria meningitidis infections. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Rifampin is available in capsule form and is taken orally. It is usually taken once daily, and the treatment duration can range from at least 3 months to as long as 2 years. For optimal effectiveness, rifampin should be taken on an empty stomach, either 1 hour before or at least 2 hours after a meal. If swallowing the capsule is difficult, the contents can be mixed with applesauce or jelly. Always follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take rifampin exactly as prescribed, without altering the dosage or frequency. Before starting rifampin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to rifampin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), cyclosporine, estrogen, hydrocortisone, medications for heart disease or diabetes, methadone, prednisone, theophylline, verapamil, and vitamins. Rifampin can reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptives, so you should use an alternative method of birth control while on this medication. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking rifampin, notify your doctor immediately. Be aware that rifampin may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate this drowsiness, so it is advisable to avoid alcohol while taking this medication. If you miss a dose of rifampin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Rifampin may cause certain side effects. A harmless but noticeable effect is the red-orange discoloration of urine, stools, saliva, sputum, sweat, and tears. Notify your doctor if any of the following mild side effects persist or worsen: headache, muscle or bone pain, heartburn, upset stomach, vomiting, stomach cramps, chills, or diarrhea. However, if you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: skin rash or hives, sores on the skin or in the mouth, fever, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (a potential sign of liver issues). Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store rifampin in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor will order tests to monitor your response to rifampin. Do not share this medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Rifampin is sold under the brand names Rifadin®, Rifadin® IV, and Rimactane®. Combination products containing rifampin include Rifamate® (rifampin and isoniazid) and Rifater® (rifampin, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide).
